\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উদ্যোগ} (udyog)}{উদ্যোগ (udyog)}]{\bn{উদ্যোগ} (udyog) — an initiative; an enterprise}

\label{lesson:BN-C498-udyog}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for dismissed, then the Bengali for to lay off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উদ্যোগ}}
\textbf{\bn{উদ্যোগ}} — \emph{udyog} — \textquotedblleft{}an initiative; an enterprise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{নতুন} \bn{উদ্যোগে} \bn{গ্রামের} \bn{মহিলারা} \bn{কাজ} \bn{পেল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ei nôtun udyoge grāmer môhilārā kāj pelô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Through this new initiative the village women found work.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উদ্যোগ}} (\emph{udyog}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{udyoga}, \textquotedblleft{}the act of undertaking something, exertion\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udyog}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udyog}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Ei nôtun udyoge grāmer môhilārā kāj pelô.} — Through this new initiative the village women found work.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for dismissed, then the Bengali for to lay off, then say \emph{udyog} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{উদ্যোগ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An initiative; an enterprise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কারবার} (kārbār)}{কারবার (kārbār)}]{\bn{কারবার} (kārbār) — a trade; a line of business}

\label{lesson:BN-C498-karbar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to lay off, then the Bengali for an initiative.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কারবার}}
\textbf{\bn{কারবার}} — \emph{kārbār} — \textquotedblleft{}a trade; a line of business\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দাদুর} \bn{কাপড়ের} \bn{কারবার} \bn{ছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dādur kāpṛer kārbār chhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather was in the cloth trade.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কারবার}} (\emph{kārbār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{kārbār}, \textquotedblleft{}business, affairs\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{kār}, \textquotedblleft{}work\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kārbār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kārbār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Dādur kāpṛer kārbār chhilô.} — My grandfather was in the cloth trade.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to lay off, then the Bengali for an initiative, then say \emph{kārbār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{কারবার} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A trade; a line of business\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পুঁজি} (pũji)}{পুঁজি (pũji)}]{\bn{পুঁজি} (pũji) — capital (money to start a business)}

\label{lesson:BN-C498-puji}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an initiative, then the Bengali for a line of business.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পুঁজি}}
\textbf{\bn{পুঁজি}} — \emph{pũji} — \textquotedblleft{}capital (money to start a business)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{নতুন} \bn{দোকানের} \bn{জন্য} \bn{আমার} \bn{পুঁজি} \bn{দরকার।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nôtun dokāner jônyô āmār pũji dôrkār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I need capital for the new shop.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পুঁজি}} (\emph{pũji}) is a tadbhava: CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{pũji}, \textquotedblleft{}a heap, capital\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{puñja}, \textquotedblleft{}a heap\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8251).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pũji}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pũji}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Nôtun dokāner jônyô āmār pũji dôrkār.} — I need capital for the new shop.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an initiative, then the Bengali for a line of business, then say \emph{pũji} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{পুঁজি} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Capital (money to start a business)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অংশীদার} (ôngshīdār)}{অংশীদার (ôngshīdār)}]{\bn{অংশীদার} (ôngshīdār) — a business partner}

\label{lesson:BN-C498-ongshidar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a line of business, then the Bengali for capital.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অংশীদার}}
\textbf{\bn{অংশীদার}} — \emph{ôngshīdār} — \textquotedblleft{}a business partner\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আমার} \bn{বন্ধু} \bn{এই} \bn{ব্যবসায়} \bn{আমার} \bn{অংশীদার।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Āmār bôndhu ei bæbsāy āmār ôngshīdār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My friend is my partner in this business.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অংশীদার}} (\emph{ôngshīdār}) joins Sanskrit \emph{aṃśa}, \textquotedblleft{}a share\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), to the Persian ending \emph{-dār}, \textquotedblleft{}one who holds\textquotedblright{}: a holder of a share.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôngshīdār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôngshīdār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Āmār bôndhu ei bæbsāy āmār ôngshīdār.} — My friend is my partner in this business.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a line of business, then the Bengali for capital, then say \emph{ôngshīdār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অংশীদার} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A business partner\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{শেয়ার} (sheyār)}{শেয়ার (sheyār)}]{\bn{শেয়ার} (sheyār) — a company share; a share}

\label{lesson:BN-C498-sheyar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for capital, then the Bengali for a business partner.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{শেয়ার}}
\textbf{\bn{শেয়ার}} — \emph{sheyār} — \textquotedblleft{}a company share; a share\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বাবা} \bn{একটা} \bn{কোম্পানির} \bn{শেয়ার} \bn{কিনলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bābā ekṭā kompānir sheyār kinlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father bought shares in a company.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{শেয়ার}} (\emph{sheyār}) is borrowed from English \emph{share}, used of a share in a company.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sheyār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sheyār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Bābā ekṭā kompānir sheyār kinlen.} — My father bought shares in a company.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for capital, then the Bengali for a business partner, then say \emph{sheyār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{শেয়ার} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A company share; a share\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
